I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It is the only file I created, and I didn't install anything. I compared outputs against the original by reading the code, not by running them, because lodash isn't installed here, so the original can't be built or run.

- **`publicFields`:** uses `pick` from `es-toolkit/object`, with the same key list as before.
- **`totalAge`:** uses `sumBy` from `es-toolkit`. It now takes a function, `(r) => r.age`, in place of lodash's `'age'` string shorthand.
- **`toLookup`:** `es-toolkit` has no `fromPairs` outside `es-toolkit/compat`. I used `zipObject(pairs.map(p => p[0]), pairs.map(p => p[1]))` instead. For duplicate names the last value wins, as in lodash `fromPairs`. No lodash import remains.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 244 bytes (min+gzip), with 129 bytes of my own code. I also tried `es-toolkit/compat`'s `fromPairs` in a scratch copy, which I've since deleted. It came to 308 bytes with 101 bytes of own code. I kept `zipObject` because it is 64 bytes smaller in the bundle. The cost is about 28 more bytes of my own code. If the own-code allowance turns out to be tight, switching to compat `fromPairs` is the alternative.

I couldn't get a size for the original `src/module.ts`, because lodash isn't installed. So I can't say how the 129 bytes compares with the original's own code.

I ran `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`. The only errors are the missing lodash modules in `src/module.ts`. Nothing was reported for `out/module.ts`.
